newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-D.C. UNITED OVERCOMES TWO-GOAL DEFICIT TO WIN MLS TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-D.C. UNITED OVERCOMES TWO-GOAL DEFICIT TO WIN MLS TITLE.

text.p: The Washington D.C. United scored three unanswered goals to overcome a two-goal deficit and beat the Los Angeles Galaxy 3-2 in extra time Sunday to capture the Major League Soccer championship.

Defender Eddie Pope scored the game-winner in the 95th minute by heading in a corner kick by Bolivian international Marco Etcheverry from eight metres. The goal sent the highly partisan crowd of 34,643 into celebration.
"It (scoring) was incredible," said Pope. "I felt the first goal that we gave up was somewhat my fault. It (corner kick) was a perfect ball, I just had to redirect it."
Etcheverry set up all three Washington goals and was the unanimous choice as the game's Most Valuable Player.
The championship match was played in driving rain with wind gusts reaching 50 miles per hour (80 kph).
Pope's goal saved the final from being decided by a shootout, which would have taken place if no goal were scored in two 15-minute extra-time sessions.
"It was a very physical game," said Etcheverry, "but both teams came to play football. We promised a championship to Washington and the real heroes are our fans that came all this way."
Nearly 5,000 fans travelled from Washington for the match.
"The fever is alive in the United States," said D.C. midfielder John Harkes, "and we put it on the map today."
Los Angeles, winners in two of three regular-season matches against Washington, led 2-0 until the 73rd minute.
Ecuadorian international Eduardo Hurtado opened the scoring in the fifth minute when he headed in a cross from Salvadoran international Mauricio Cienfuegos from eight metres out along the left post.

In the 55th minute, Galaxy midfielder Chris Armas worked between D.C. defenders Jeff Agoos and Mario Gori before hitting a left-footed shot that beat goalkeeper Mark Simpson (two saves) along the left post from 16 metres.
Washington coach Bruce Arena brought on two attacking players in the second half in a move that paid dividends.
Once forward Tony Sannah and midfielder Shawn Medved replaced midfielder John Maessner and defender Mario Gori, Washington enjoyed the complete run of play.
At 73 minutes Sannah headed in Etcheverry's indirect free kick to bring Washington within a goal.

The goal was set up after Galaxy defender Arash Noamouz' hard tackle on Jaime Moreno gave the United a free kick from about 25 metres out on the left side. Etcheverry's left-footed restart found Sannah, who headed home.
D.C. leveled the score at 82 minutes when Medved finished off his own rebound from 10 metres.

Etcheverry again played a vital role with a curling free kick from the left side that was punched out by Campos only to have Medved one-time a sizzling shot. Campos blocked it but Medved latched onto the rebound for the equaliser.
"Etcheverry and his bent balls ruined the whole day for us," said Galaxy coach Lothar Osiander. "But then again, he's a world-class player."
The Galaxy had won the Western Conference title with a 19-13 record. D.C. United finished second in the Eastern Conference with a 16-16 mark during the regular season.

A waterlogged field made play difficult for each team. In many cases, opportunities that may have produced goals in drier playing conditions became botched attempts as players overran balls or mistimed shots.
Washington, peaking at the right time in the MLS inaugural season, held the edge in shots (14-5) and corner kicks (7-3).
"We became a team over the course of the season," said Arena, who also coached the U.S. Olympic team.
